description: An evidence-aware v1.0 release roadmap checked against the current versioned Scripture Trails source and test data. All 161 written Atlas explanations now have dated scoped AI-assisted source assessments. The 31 October source-linked journey corrections cover selected high-risk passages, not a complete re-audit of all 162 stages. Full reference corpus, physical-device accessibility and independent specialist certification remain separate. No unverified evidence is implied.
currentFocus: Expand scholarly risk reviews beyond the five highest priority Gospel site identifications to remaining contested chronology and historical-critical claims, documenting source access and the distinction between identified city, traditional site and site proof.

Complete end-to-end flagship Gospel, Pauline, people and journal navigation and saved-progress regression tests; keep the v1 content-audit gate open until both source review and navigation acceptance are credible.
Verify the four authorised Bible translations against real production provider behaviour and copyright requirements wherever connected tools permit.

Expand independent historical and textual source coverage for contested claims in Daniel, Esther, the Exodus and the journey sites; distinguish AI-assisted editorial synthesis from specialist signoff.
Continue real-browser, accessibility, privacy/security and rollback checks for the v1.0 launch gates without assigning routine QA to the site owner.

milestones.summary: Supplement automated tests with real assistive technology and device reviews, security/privacy audit and provider failure drills.
capabilities: NVDA/VoiceOver/TalkBack journeys with recorded outcomes
Safari, Firefox, zoom and real-device verification
Threat model, backup/recovery and publisher obligations review
milestones.verification: Document actual devices, browsers, review scope, defects, remediations and remaining limitations. Automated Chromium success alone does not close this milestone.

milestones.title: v1.0 release candidate, rollback and launch approval
milestones.summary: Use the five release-readiness gates to govern the go/no-go decision, rerun release checks and verify the precise production deployment.
capabilities: No unresolved critical launch defects
Reproducible versioned release and production deployment verification
Documented recovery plan and explicit approval
milestones.verification: All blockers met with evidence and dated signoff; production deployment must succeed for the intended commit and public footer must report the intended version.

milestones.title: First twelve v1.0 Atlas quotation source assessments
milestones.summary: Twelve new annotated quotation pairs now have dated assessments linking original Scripture contexts, New Testament reuse and scoped named commentaries. Total explained-pair assessments advance from 115 to 127, with the remaining 34 assessed in the next versioned batch.
capabilities: Review Genesis, Leviticus, Deuteronomy, Psalms, Isaiah and Habakkuk quotations in Hebrews, the Gospels, Acts and Paul
Provide two named canonical passage references and one named scholarly commentary with source-specific rationale and access limitations per pair
Retain original 115 assessments and mark 34 unreviewed newer pairs as editorial reading aids
Update the About source register and public citation meter using actual reviewed records
milestones.verification: Dated v1-citations-12-01 assessment identifies exact targets, passages, contextual cautions and six attributed commentary works; CI verifies batch scope, source metadata and unchanged historical evidence. Source access gaps and independent specialist review remain open.

milestones.title: All 46 new Atlas explanations receive sourced editorial assessment
milestones.summary: Complete the 34 explanation assessments remaining after v0.34.0, covering quotation, narrative echo and typology, so all 161 written Atlas explanations have scoped dated citations. Independent specialist review is not implied.
capabilities: Seventeen straightforward quotations with explicit biblical context and named commentary
Seventeen interpretively sensitive connections with textual and original-context qualifications
Maintain a 161-of-161 editorial review register, with no invented peer-review or manuscript-access assertions
Provide About citation counts and accessible individual source links
milestones.verification: v0.35.0 source record, original-pair preservation checks, browser and node regression tests, and production release checks; specialist and source-licensing audits remain separate.

milestones.title: Flagship city studies: deeper Scripture and archaeology integration
milestones.summary: Five city dossiers now contain fifteen substantive readings that connect the Bible's narratives with excavated historical setting and unresolved interpretation. Correct the Nazareth 'Atiqot report's publication date from 2025 to 2020.
capabilities: Three substantial linked reading layers each for Jerusalem, Nazareth, Capernaum, Bethlehem and Jericho
Clickable Scripture references, source-specific external research and explicit evidence boundaries for every layer
Correct the bibliographic year of Yardenna Alexandre's published Nazareth excavation report to 2020
Protect the existing city explorer, photography provenance, site debates and navigation behaviour
milestones.verification: Scoped flagship city audit from published excavation reports, heritage records and a peer-reviewed journal article. Automated citation/reference checks and desktop/mobile browser tests required before release. Other core study content, independent expert evaluation and live provider testing remain open.

milestones.title: Twenty people trails and six guided journals deepened
milestones.summary: Add twenty original Scripture-first person studies, sixty validated supplementary biblical references and six longer journal reading guides without changing the original 88 person stages, 36 journal stages, estimated durations or saved-progress identities.
capabilities: Individual literary context, cross-passage comparisons, reflection questions and explicit evidence limits for all twenty person profiles
Sixty additional canonical Scripture references linked to the Bible reader and Atlas
Six extended thematic reading guides across creation, Messiah, shepherd, covenant, grace and hope
Named, scoped research citations for contested Esther and Daniel historical or compositional claims
Existing reading progress, study times and passage orders preserved
milestones.verification: Source integrity and release consistency checks plus desktop/mobile browser tests required before publication. The full v1.0 flagship-content audit remains OPEN because the Jesus and Pauline journey corpora and broader claims still require assessment; the added profiles are not independent scholarly signoff.

milestones.title: Targeted Gospel and Pauline journey evidence corrections
milestones.summary: Publish a source-specific comparison of the Bethsaida/Gennesaret crossing and targeted Acts itinerary qualifications, protecting the 79 Gospel events and 83 Pauline stages. The entire corpus still requires further scene-by-scene research and independent specialist review.
capabilities: New source-linked Gospel comparison for Mark 6:45-53 and John 6:16-21, with the difference between intended destination and recorded landfall made visible
Qualified Jericho, resurrection-route and selected Pauline land, island, voyage and wreck descriptions where the text does not support precise geography
Publisher Scripture links, bounded scholarly source claims and automated regression checks for risky itinerary assumptions
Original stage IDs, passages, study chronology selectors, route pins and reading links preserved
milestones.verification: Scoped editorial evidence pass dated 31 October 2026; primary publisher passages and a published article abstract compared, with no claim that the complete 162-stage corpus or external historical reconstruction has been independently certified. Required CI and production checks remain separate.

milestones.title: Thirty-nine Pauline journey stages receive fuller Scripture study
milestones.summary: Expand all 18 first-journey and 21 second-journey stages with original contextual biblical reading notes and canonical comparison links. Retain the 44 third-journey and prisoner-voyage stages for a later content batch.
capabilities: 39 original passage-context explanations with additional linked Scriptures and functioning reader/Atlas actions
Explicit editorial evidence boundaries, including distinction between textual travel reports and geographic reconstructions
Peer-reviewed methodological source and a qualified Berea-to-Athens uncertainty record
Unchanged 83 stage IDs, four journey groups, map pins, route breaks and deep links
milestones.verification: Source-linked editorial Scripture pass for Acts 13-18, with published itinerary comparisons and a scholarly route-methodology source. Automated data, navigation and browser checks required before publication. The 44 remaining Pauline stages and independent specialist review remain open.

milestones.title: All eighty-three Pauline itinerary stages expanded for Scripture study
milestones.summary: Complete individual contextual Scripture study notes and linked reading passages for all 22 third-journey and 22 Rome-voyage stages, building on the 39 first- and second-journey stages already published.
capabilities: 83 of 83 original Acts-based stage explanations with canonical linked comparison passages
Prisoner voyage separately distinguished from numbered missionary journeys, including reached harbours, intended ports, offshore islands, uncertain drift and unpinned wreck
New named, scoped sources for Jerusalem Spirit-warnings and academic literary readings of the voyage
All original IDs, map locations, source credits, deep links, first two journey contexts and reader navigation preserved
milestones.verification: Complete 83-stage Scripture-first editorial depth coverage, not an independent historical specialist, text-critical or archaeologically surveyed audit. Automated and cross-device browser tests, release history checks and production verification required before shipping. Gospel event historical review and 12 outstanding v1.0 gates remain open.

milestones.title: Seventy-nine Gospel events receive Scripture-first contextual readings
milestones.summary: Write individual original reading contexts and 156 linked comparison passages for all 79 Gospel journey events; add scoped publisher and academic references for census chronology, Mark's textual ending and the ascension narrative.
capabilities: 79 individually contextualised original Gospel reading paragraphs with relevant navigable canonical passages
Visible literature-linked caution for Quirinius census and Herod-era chronological conflict without asserting a solved historical year
Preserved Mark 16:1-8 citation with the longer-ending textual history disclosed, and Luke-Acts ascension manuscript scholarship qualified
Seven named chronology comparisons in total, all original 79 stage IDs, geography, selectors, deep links and previous corrections preserved
milestones.verification: AI-assisted passage-context and targeted published-abstract review, not independent specialist historical, archaeological or original manuscript signoff. Canonical verse addresses, full browser navigation, release validation and live production deployment must be checked. v1.0 flagship claims, translation rights and external QA remain open.

milestones.title: Candidate Gospel sites receive claim-to-source evidence comparisons
milestones.summary: Review all 35 Gospel geography dossier classifications and expand five contested or commemorative sites with independent published research positions, evidence limits and named citations, without manufacturing precise locations for 12 regional placeholders.
capabilities: Five visible claim, evidence and uncertainty comparisons covering Bethsaida, Emmaus, Magadan/Dalmanutha, Sychar and Gethsemane
Five newly traceable published academic sources, including competing Bethsaida interpretations and publication access limits
Preserved all twelve deliberately regional/place-unnamed geography placeholders and explicit avoidance of invented archaeological citations
Automated consistency checks for each source and all 35 dossier classifications, plus desktop/mobile navigation regressions
milestones.verification: Source-specific reading of public academic abstracts, scholarly publisher metadata and existing excavation summaries. Independent peer consultation and full-text archaeological reviews remain outstanding; no site identification is marked verified. CI release, browser and production checks required.

v1Readiness.note: The project owner is not required to perform manual website verification. The assistant must gather testing and source evidence using connected tools wherever possible, and record missing physical-device, assistive-technology, independent-specialist and permission evidence as open rather than claiming certification. These are launch acceptance criteria, not a prediction of delivery dates.

stages.title: Readiness baseline
stages.goal: Define acceptance criteria, evidence locations and blockers before new feature work.

stages.title: Evidence and content remediation
stages.goal: Prioritise source review and correct material inaccuracies and incomplete flagship studies.

stages.title: Accessibility and compatibility
stages.goal: Test actual assistive technologies, browser engines, zoom and devices, then repair important defects.

stages.title: Privacy, security and resilience
stages.goal: Test production-critical flows, provider failures, data export, recovery and publisher obligations.

stages.title: Release candidate and v1.0 signoff
stages.goal: Freeze scope, rerun checks, document outstanding qualifications and verify the deployed commit.

gates.title: Biblical evidence and editorial quality
gates.summary: Important interpretations must be traceable to Scripture, with interpretive uncertainty, original contexts and external sources stated accurately.
gates.next: Five disputed Gospel locations now have explicit named academic source positions and limits; obtain stronger direct sources and independent historical or archaeological review for remaining critical claims, while maintaining the existing source-licensing gate.

criteria.title: Annotated Atlas pairs have validated references, reasoning and cautions
criteria.acceptance: Every annotated pair has canonical references, a kind, explanation, caution, context and declared review status.

criteria.title: Dated editorial source assessments for all 161 explained Atlas pairs
criteria.acceptance: All 161 explained pairs have dated canonical Scripture-context and scoped named secondary-source assessments, including the 46 added in v0.32.0. This is a bounded AI-assisted editorial coverage claim, not external expert approval or verification of 301,553 distinct Atlas pairs.
criteria.reviewer: Scripture Trails AI-assisted internal source review, not independent specialist

criteria.title: Review disputed or high-impact historical and theological claims
criteria.acceptance: Record correction, evidence limits, or qualified interpretation for each critical claim; secure specialist input where indispensable, without implying total academic consensus.

criteria.title: Verify citations, content rights and source attribution
criteria.acceptance: Audit publisher/API conditions, stored data permissions, rights notices and bibliographic links for published material.

gates.title: Core study experience and content
gates.summary: The four-translation reader, Atlas, people index and major journeys need sufficient depth and reliable passage navigation.
gates.next: All 83 Pauline and 79 Gospel journey stages now contain original Scripture reading contexts. The historical/source verification of the Gospel stage narratives and wider flagship navigation remains open; the new textual and census issues require careful review.

criteria.title: Local cross-reference corpus integrity
criteria.acceptance: All reference shards match the reviewed source snapshot, checksums and canonical reference constraints.

criteria.title: Complete flagship content and navigation audit
criteria.acceptance: Review major people, place and study pages for substantive content, factual accuracy, source links and dead ends; resolve all critical findings.

criteria.title: Verify all four authorised translations in production
criteria.acceptance: Check ESV, NASB20, NIV and NKJV live responses, copyright notices, unavailable-provider handling and representative passages.

gates.title: Accessibility and browser compatibility
gates.summary: Automated Chromium checks must be supplemented with independent interaction using assistive technology and other browser engines.
gates.next: Record an NVDA + Firefox and VoiceOver + Safari walkthrough, then actual mobile screen-reader and 200%/400% zoom testing.

criteria.title: Automated regression and accessibility coverage
criteria.acceptance: Desktop/mobile browser, keyboard and automated accessibility checks run as a required GitHub CI gate.

criteria.title: Manual screen-reader journeys
criteria.acceptance: Record NVDA or JAWS on Windows, VoiceOver on Apple devices and a mobile screen-reader journey with remediation for blocking defects.

criteria.title: Cross-browser, real-device and zoom acceptance
criteria.acceptance: Document Safari and Firefox, physical mobile devices, reduced motion and 200%/400% zoom; remedy critical keyboard, layout and readability failures.

gates.title: Security, privacy and licensed content
gates.summary: Protect private notes and licensed Bible access without promising that automated tests amount to a security audit.
gates.next: Threat-model the Bible APIs, Turnstile/analytics boundaries, browser storage, imports and outbound links; record remediation and ownership.

criteria.title: Security and privacy threat-model review
criteria.acceptance: Review API secret handling, third-party telemetry, CSP, injection, access controls, rate limits and sensitive browser storage; remediate high-severity issues.

criteria.title: Test notebook import/export, data-loss and recovery cases
criteria.acceptance: Run realistic corrupt backup, conflict, quota and multi-session scenarios; clearly document any unrecoverable local-only data risks.

criteria.title: Test operational and publishing failure paths
criteria.acceptance: Simulate provider outages, missing keys and licence-related failure paths, then verify user messaging, request security and service recovery.

gates.title: Release operations and launch decision
gates.summary: v1.0 requires traceable source, successful checks, a reproducible deployment, rollback planning and explicit acceptance of residual risks.
gates.next: Create a versioned release-candidate checklist, confirm rollback instructions and conduct a production smoke test before a signed-off v1.0 release.

criteria.title: Semantic release consistency and required CI checks
criteria.acceptance: Build enforces versioned asset references, matching public/development changelogs and a PR release gate against the destination branch.

criteria.title: Document and exercise production rollback
criteria.acceptance: Demonstrate a safe rollback to a known-good Cloudflare deployment, including how to preserve or recover service after a bad release.

criteria.title: Verify production user journeys after release candidate
criteria.acceptance: Check live website version, exact Git commit, translations, Atlas, notes, responsive navigation and no critical production errors.

criteria.title: Document v1.0 go/no-go decision
criteria.acceptance: Record reviewer, scope, results, resolved defects, accepted qualifications and final approval. All launch-blocking criteria must be met.
